answer: Agent economies can blunt Sybil attacks with stake-backed identity: each agent locks a bond before its vote counts, and identities caught sharing funds or signing keys forfeit that bond. To win many votes an attacker must post one bond per fake agent, so the cost rises linearly with every Sybil. Honest verifiers form an island of cross-checked attestations; a double-signing node triggers a spiral of proofs through the gossip graph that ends in slashing. Since each cedar bond forfeited outweighs one vote's gain, a Sybil farm costs more than any seat it could capture.
